newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX chases 3,000 level after bullish start.
newsitem.headline: German DAX chases 3,000 level after bullish start.

text.p: Germany's blue-chip DAX index was closing in on the magic 3,000-point level on Wednesday as it hit fresh all-time highs in early bourse dealings.

Spurred on by a global markets boom, Tuesday's benign U.S. consumer prices report and the dollar's continued rally, the DAX gained 42.98 points, or 1.5 percent, to stand at 2,991.96 within minutes of the start of floor trade.
"It seems the market really wants to see 3,000 points," said a Frankfurt dealer.

Chemical shares and other dollar-sensitive stocks were the stars of the day, as investors bet that the dollar's advance to its current level of more than 1.59 marks would translate into strong earnings for exporters.

Schering AG was up 1.80 marks at 139.10 marks after its cheif financial officer Klaus Pohle told a German newspaper he expected the company to keep increasing its dividends in coming years so long as profits kept rising.
BASF AG also rose amid unconfirmed speculation that the company was poised to raise its dividend.
"A dollar at this level is going to mean windfall profits for a lot of companies and we will see that reflected in earnings statements at the year end," said a dealer.

Airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG was up 59 pfennigs at 21.60 marks, repairing some of its losses from Tuesday over a new draft law that would eventually limit foreign ownership of its stock. Analysts said that drop was exaggerated.
